title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 213 (Investigation into company’s affairs in other cases)

content.overview: Section 213 empowers the Tribunal to order investigation into the affairs of a company on an application by members meeting the prescribed threshold (or by other persons as the section allows), where the business is being conducted with intent to defraud creditors, members or any other person, or otherwise for a fraudulent or unlawful purpose, or where persons concerned in formation or management have been guilty of fraud, misfeasance or other misconduct. The Tribunal may also order investigation on application by any other person or otherwise if circumstances suggest that the business is being conducted as above. The order is made to the Central Government, which then appoints inspectors. This is distinct from the Central Government’s own power under section 210 and from SFIO assignment under section 212.
content.glance: Tribunal may order investigation on member application (threshold, unless waived) or other persons; grounds: intent to defraud, unlawful purpose, fraud/misfeasance/misconduct; order to CG to appoint inspectors; distinct from ss. 210 and 212.
content.study: The Tribunal may, on an application made by not less than one hundred members or members holding not less than one-tenth of the total voting power (or such other number as may be prescribed), or on an application by any other person or otherwise, if it is satisfied that there are circumstances suggesting that—(a) the business of the company is being conducted with intent to defraud its creditors, members or any other person, or otherwise for a fraudulent or unlawful purpose, or in a manner oppressive to any of its members, or that the company was formed for any fraudulent or unlawful purpose; or (b) persons concerned in the formation or management have been guilty of fraud, misfeasance or other misconduct towards the company or its members, order investigation into the affairs of the company. The Central Government shall appoint inspectors on such order. Current-law framing: test standing (member threshold or other person); establish the statutory circumstances (defraud, unlawful purpose, fraud/misfeasance/misconduct); Tribunal order; CG appoints inspectors. Distinct from CG-initiated investigation under s. 210 and SFIO under s. 212.

sections.heading: Standing
sections.body: Application by members meeting the numerical or voting-power threshold (unless the Tribunal waives), or by any other person, or otherwise as the section allows.

sections.heading: Grounds
sections.body: Circumstances suggesting business conducted with intent to defraud, or for fraudulent/unlawful purpose, or oppressive; or formation/management persons guilty of fraud, misfeasance or misconduct.

sections.heading: Order and Follow-Through
sections.body: Tribunal orders investigation; Central Government appoints inspectors.

sections.heading: Relationship to Other Routes
sections.body: Distinct from CG’s own power under s. 210 and SFIO assignment under s. 212.

provisions.title: Investigation into company’s affairs in other cases

examples.title: Member-threshold application
examples.body: One hundred members apply to the Tribunal alleging that the business is being conducted with intent to defraud creditors. If the Tribunal is satisfied that the statutory circumstances exist, it may order investigation under s. 213; the Central Government then appoints inspectors.

examples.title: Not the same as s. 210
examples.body: Members cannot assume that a s. 213 application is decided by the Central Government. The Tribunal decides whether to order investigation; the Central Government’s role under s. 213 is to appoint inspectors after the Tribunal’s order.

hypotheticals.question: Must the Central Government itself be satisfied of fraud before a s. 213 investigation can begin?
hypotheticals.analysis: Under s. 213 the Tribunal must be satisfied that the statutory circumstances exist and then order investigation. The Central Government’s function on that order is to appoint inspectors. Separately, the Central Government may itself order investigation under s. 210 on its own triggers.

distinctions.title: Tribunal-ordered investigation (s. 213) vs CG investigation (s. 210)
distinctions.left: Tribunal orders on member/other application; CG appoints inspectors
distinctions.right: CG itself orders on s. 208 report, special resolution, public interest, or department request

misconceptions.trap: Any single member can always force a Tribunal investigation order under s. 213.
misconceptions.correction: Member applications must meet the numerical or voting-power threshold unless the Tribunal waives it. Other persons may apply as the section allows, but the Tribunal must still be satisfied of the statutory circumstances.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 213 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Test standing (threshold or other person). II. Establish statutory circumstances. III. Tribunal order; CG appoints inspectors. IV. Distinguish ss. 210/212. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Standing; circumstances; order sought; precise relief.
